newsitem.title: USA: Ford idles two car plants next week.
newsitem.headline: Ford idles two car plants next week.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Thursday it will idle production next week at its Lorain, Ohio, and Wixom, Canada, car assembly plants.

About 1,450 hourly workers will be affected at the Lorain plant, which normally makes 3,200 Thunderbird and Mercury Cougar models per week. Ford has said it will stop production of those models later this year.

The Wixom facility will begin a production changeover for its 1998 Lincoln Town Car and Lincoln Continental next week, followed by a two-week vacation and then another week of downtime beginning July 14, with production resuming July 21.
Ford said several assembly plants will be working daily overtime this week, including Wayne, Mich.; Kansas City; Louisville, Ky.; Norfolk, Va.; Oakville, Ontario; and St. Louis.

General Motors Corp announced it would have overtime of two hours each day from June 23 through June 26 at its Wilmington, Del., Chevrolet Malibu car plant and its Fort Wayne, Ind., full-size pickup truck plant.
Chrysler Corp. said its Newark, Del., will not operate next week due to model changeover.

The automaker said its Toledo, Ohio, will operate two eight-hour shifts during the week and one four-hour shift on Saturday, June 21. Its Dodge City Complex in Warren, Mich., and St. Louis-North in Fenton, Mo., will operate two nine-hour shifts during the week and two eight-hour shifts on Saturday, June 21.

In Ontario, Canada, Chrysler's Windsor assembly plant will operate three seven-and-a-half hour shifts during the week. Bramalea and Pillette will operate two eight-hour shifts during the week and two eight hour shifts on Saturday, June 21.
